$comment: Pre-registration of the change-impact measurement (#582, epic #572). Supersedes code-awareness-roi.json registration_version 3, which is kept as the record of the completed v3 run and stays reproducible from ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2 with evaluate.mjs. Thresholds decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18. Fixed BEFORE any v4 scenario has been run; the two pilot commits named under sample.excluded_pilot were run against the plumbing only and are excluded from the sample. Amending anything after the main run has started invalidates that run: bump registration_version and say which version a report belongs to.
registered_by: Claude Opus 5; thresholds decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18
why_a_new_registration: v3 answered its question and the answer invalidated its own comparison: `find_code` was offered in 44 of 44 runs and called in 0, so both arms ran the same grep behaviour and the measured difference (+0.8 Pp recall) is noise between two runs of one procedure. Two things were confounded — whether an agent REACHES for the graph, and whether the graph's answer HELPS. This design separates them into three arms.
question: (a) Adoption: offered a change-impact tool described graph-first, how often does an agent call it? (b) Effect: when the change-impact answer is in front of the agent, does it name more of the files the change really breaks, without naming more wrong ones and without costing disproportionate context?

A.name: grep
A.description: No MCP server at all — text search and file reads only. Identical to v3's control arm.

B.name: offered
B.description: `find_code` and `find_affected_files` offered over stdio MCP, nothing else changed. Whether the agent calls them is the observation.

prefilled.name: prefilled
prefilled.description: The same tools, plus the `find_affected_files` answer for exactly the planned change already in the prompt. The information is guaranteed to have been SHOWN; nothing forces the agent to use it, which is why the arm is not called `forced`.
prefilled.symbols_from: the product's own `changedSymbolsOf` applied to the scenario diff — not a hand-written list, so both graph arms start from the information the prompt already carries

arms.mcp_server: packages/eval/code-roi/v2/code-tools-mcp.mjs (the product's own tool definitions and handlers)
arms.isolation: unchanged from v3: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence`, a fresh process per scenario and arm, cwd a throwaway worktree with no `.git`, the graph moved out of the tree so no arm can read it as a file
arms.tools: Read and read-only shell search; no edits, no subagents, no web
arms.arm_order: randomized per scenario by the registered seed, written into the scenario file before the first run

unit_and_truth.unit: one historical change to one file, at most one scenario per file
unit_and_truth.ground_truth: a file is affected when it carries a type error after applying exactly that file's diff that it did not carry before; errors compared as (file, TS code, message) multisets with line and column ignored; adjudicated by hand before any arm runs, removals only with a written reason
unit_and_truth.$comment: The truth definition is not touched. Changing the ruler and the tool in the same step would leave nothing comparable.

primary_metric.name: affected_file_recall
primary_metric.definition: Per scenario: |named ∩ truth| / |truth|, `named` being the JSON array on the last FILES: line of the final answer, normalized to repo-relative POSIX paths.
primary_metric.compared: prefilled against A, paired per scenario

context_metric.name: input_tokens
context_metric.definition: Per arm, from the run's own `result` event: modelUsage[claude-sonnet-5].inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens. All three are summed because a cached token is a token the model read. Side models the client calls on its own (haiku for titles and the like) are excluded — they are not the agent's context and differ between arms at random. Fallback when modelUsage is absent: the run-level `usage` block summed the same way, and the row is marked `usageFallback`.
context_metric.$comment: v3 counted characters of TOOL RESULTS. That rule is blind to the prompt, and the prefilled arm's block arrives in the prompt — under it the arm that spends the most context would have scored as free. This is the correction the v4 design needs to be honest about its own cost.

verdicts.$comment: TWO verdicts, decided separately, with no combined status. Decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18. A tool nobody calls whose answer would have helped, and a tool everyone calls whose answer does not, are opposite findings needing opposite work — one word covering both would hide which it was. Each verdict is pass, fail, underpowered (fewer than min_scenarios) or not_evaluable.

adoption.question: Does an agent offered the tool call it?

effect.question: Does the answer, once shown, make the agent name more of the breaking files without more wrong ones and without disproportionate context?
effect.$comment: All four of these must hold for the effect verdict to pass; none of them touches the adoption verdict.

thresholds.$comment: Decided by Daniel Nevoigt, 2026-09-18. Grouped into the two verdicts above; the numbers are unchanged from the first registration of this design.
thresholds.$comment_adoption: In arm B, at least 70 % of scenarios must call `find_affected_files` at least once. `find_code` calls are reported but do NOT count towards this: an agent that locates a symbol has not asked what breaks.
thresholds.$comment_recall: Mean paired difference prefilled − A of at least 5 percentage points, AND the lower bound of its 95 % bootstrap interval above 0.
thresholds.$comment_precision: Mean paired difference in precision (prefilled − A) not below −0.05.
thresholds.$comment_context: On scenarios solved in BOTH arms (recall ≥ 0.8), median prefilled input tokens at most 1.25 × median A. The restriction to scenarios both arms solved is INHERITED from registration 3, where its reason is recorded: cost is compared only where both got the answer, so a cheap wrong answer cannot win on cost. The unfiltered ratio over every scenario is reported alongside it as `notGated.context_ratio_all_scenarios`.

not_gated.context_ratio_all_scenarios: The context ratio over every scenario, not just the ones both arms solved. Reported, never gated.
not_gated.b_vs_a: Arm B against arm A is reported and never gated: it multiplies adoption and effect, and an agent that never calls the tool makes B identical to A. Reporting it as the effect is what made the v3 report unreadable.
not_gated.latency_and_hook_block: Both stay with registration 3 and come from lane telemetry (`bastra logs --stats`), not from these runs.

sample.$comment_fresh: MANDATORY. The 44 scenarios in ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2 were used to develop the symbol query this measures (entry specificity, the package-import narrowing threshold, the file-count cap were all decided against those gaps). A number from them is a training number and must not appear as an effect estimate.
sample.commit_range: non-merge commits reachable from 61652b6 (the parent of the OLDEST commit v3 used), walked NEWEST first — `mine.mjs --since 61652b6`. main's tip IS v3's range end 5483f56, so there is no newer history to take: a disjoint sample has to come from before v3's oldest scenario, and that boundary is what makes it disjoint.

excluded_pilot.$comment: Run against the plumbing before the registration was frozen. Excluded from the main sample; if the miner selects either file again from either commit, the scenario is dropped.
excluded_pilot.enforced_by: select.mjs drops any candidate from these commits before writing the scenario file — the rule is mechanical, not a note someone has to remember.
excluded_pilot.$comment_commits: The two pilot scenarios, run on 2026-09-18 against the plumbing only (archive ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4-pilot, $0.99, six arms, all evaluable). Their result is not evidence: n = 2, and the run existed to prove the pipeline, not to measure.

sample.$comment_size: 40 independent changes, above v3's 30: the effect threshold is half of v3's, so the sample carries more of the burden. Fewer than 40 qualifying scenarios → the report says `underpowered` (18.1), not a verdict.

statistics.method: paired bootstrap, 10 000 resamples, resampling by changed file with replacement

run_conditions.per_scenario_base: the commit's parent SHA, recorded in the scenario file with the graph's sha256
run_conditions.$comment_cost: Enforced by the runner, not documented at it: every finished arm's `total_cost_usd` is summed and the next arm only starts while the ceiling is still out of reach at the running average cost per arm. Raising it is a decision, not a flag someone reaches for at 2 a.m. (CODE_ROI_COST_CEILING).
run_conditions.frozen_archive: ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2 is never written by a v4 script — `archive.mjs` refuses it, because the v3 report is only reproducible while that archive is untouched.

archive.location: the directory named by CODE_ROI_OUT for the run
contents: scenario file with base SHAs, arm order and seed
raw stream-json transcript of every arm run
the prefilled block handed to the third arm, per scenario

reporting_duties: Adoption from arm B, with its N, separately for find_affected_files and find_code.
Effect from prefilled against A: paired mean with its 95 % interval, and the per-scenario rows.
Precision and context (input tokens) as defined above.
B against A, labelled as adoption and effect combined, never as the effect.
The cost of the run against the ceiling.
That the offline figures on the v3 sample (recall 91.3 %, precision 52.4 %) are development data and carry no weight here.
Both verdicts separately — adoption and effect — and never a combined status.
An honest `underpowered` / `not_evaluable` per 18.1 where the sample does not support a verdict.
The registration_version the report belongs to.
$comment_failure: A missed threshold is recorded as the finding; thresholds are not moved afterwards.
